correctness.rationale: For e_i e_j=e_(2j−i), bilinear commutator [e_i,e_j]=e_(2j−i)−e_(2i−j). Trilinearity reduces Jacobi to all basis triples. Independently expanded J(0,1,2) as +e_-5−e_-4−e_-3+e_-2−e_4+e_5+e_6−e_7, whose eight indices are distinct modulo every n>=13, so its ±1 coefficient excludes all characteristics. Independently exhaustive integer enumeration of every ordered i,j,k for 1<=n<=12 gave Jacobi coefficient gcds [0,0,0,2,1,1,1,1,3,1,1,1], proving exactly all p and moduli in theorem. In n=9, differences among each of three residue classes modulo 3 generate a 2D augmentation-zero space each, so derived Lie algebra dimension six and bracket nonzero in char3. This is a finite *complete* remainder combined with universal witness; no large-n inference from finite samples.
